newsitem.title: ITALY: Progress made in welfare talks, union head says.
newsitem.headline: Progress made in welfare talks, union head says.

text.p: The head of Italy's largest union said on Tuesday progress has been made in welfare reform talks and a union-backed solution is possible when talks resume after a summer break.

"We have noticed a step forward in our negotiations, and it is possible that the resumption of talks will lead to a solution that will have our consent," Sergio Cofferati, leader of Italy's CGIL union said.

Guglielmo Epifani, Cgil's number two official, said at a meeting on Tuesday closing the first round of welfare talks before summer holidays, Prime Minister Romano Prodi presented a "satisfying and correct" document.
At the meeting, Prodi and representatives of 31 union and employer groups decided talks would resume on August 28, with the thorny pension reforms issue topping the agenda.
Prodi launched the welfare review, which aims to secure an agreement on reducing social spending to help Italy qualify for the first round of Europe's single currency, in mid-June.

The government hopes an agreement on reforms will coincide with the 1998 budget presentation to parliament. The budget must be presented to legislators by September 30. -- Rome newsroom +39 6 678 2501
